problem:
The rate at which the population of a particular country grows $P(t),$ after $t$ years, can be modeled by the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}P}{\text{d}t}=0.02P.
$$

How many years does it take for the population to double? Round your answer to the nearest year.
worked_solution:
We model the population growth using the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}P}{\text{d}t}=0.02P.
$$

The solution to this equation is

$$
P(t)={P}_{0}\,{e}^{0.02t},
$$

where ${P}_{0}$ is the initial population.

Let ${t}_{1}$ be the time when the population of the country is double the initial number. That is,

$$
P({t}_{1})=2{P}_{0}.
$$

We solve the above equation for ${t}_{1},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P({t}_{1}) & ={P}_{0}{e}^{0.02\cdot {t}_{1}} \\ 2{P}_{0} & ={P}_{0}{e}^{0.02{t}_{1}} \\ 2 & ={e}^{0.02{t}_{1}} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡2 & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{0.02{t}_{1}}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡2 & =0.02{t}_{1} \\ {t}_{1} & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{0.02} \\ {t}_{1} & ≈34.657\end{aligned}
$$

Rounding to the nearest integer, we conclude that it takes $35$ years for the population to double.
